Decisions: Jim Brewer takes the win for Los Angeles (1.0 IP, 4 BF, 1 H, 1 R, 1 ER, 3 SO, 1 HR) and is charged with the blown save; Sergio Romo takes the loss for San Francisco (1.0 IP, 8 BF, 5 H, 4 R, 4 ER, 1 SO, 1 HR); Clem Labine takes the save (3.0 IP, 13 BF, 1 H, 0 R, 3 BB, 2 SO), three scoreless innings to finish. Sandy Koufax started for Los Angeles (5.0 IP, 19 BF, 1 H, 3 R, 3 ER, 2 BB, 1 HBP, 3 SO, 1 HR) and Christy Mathewson started for San Francisco (5.2 IP, 23 BF, 6 H, 3 R, 3 ER, 6 SO, 1 HR); Hoyt Wilhelm finished for San Francisco (2.1 IP, 15 BF, 5 H, 6 R, 6 ER, 3 BB, 2 SO, 1 HR). Duke Snider is the export's player of the game (3 for 4, 2 2B, 1 HR, 4 RBI, 3 R, 1 BB). Scoring: the bottom of the 2nd, Barry Bonds hit a solo home run off Koufax, 1-0 San Francisco. The top of the 4th, Shohei Ohtani singled and Snider hit a two-run home run off Mathewson, 2-1 Los Angeles. The top of the 6th, Snider doubled off Mathewson with two out, Sergio Romo relieved, and Gil Hodges doubled Snider home, 3-1. The bottom of the 6th scored three and put San Francisco ahead: Art Fletcher was hit by Koufax's pitch, stole second, Willie Mays walked, Jim Brewer relieved Koufax, Will Clark and Mel Ott struck out, and Bonds hit a three-run home run off Brewer, 4-3 San Francisco; the first two runs are charged to Koufax as his inherited runners and the third, Bonds himself, to Brewer, whose printed line (1 H, 1 ER) is the home run alone. The top of the 7th scored six and decided the game: Ron Cey struck out, Pee Wee Reese doubled, Jackie Robinson's single scored Reese to tie it, Pedro Guerrero pinch-hit for Zack Wheat and singled, Mookie Betts flied out, and Ohtani hit a three-run home run off Romo; Hoyt Wilhelm relieved Romo, walked Snider, and Hodges hit a two-run home run, 9-4. Romo's four runs are Reese, Robinson, Guerrero and Ohtani; Wilhelm's first two are Snider and Hodges. The top of the 8th scored four more off Wilhelm: Cey tripled, Reese walked, Robinson's forceout scored Cey, Guerrero singled, Betts's single scored Reese, Ohtani walked, and Snider's double scored Guerrero and Betts, 13-4. Labine closed it: Jeff Kent's double in the bottom of the 9th was San Francisco's only hit after the 6th, and no Giant reached third base against him. The extra list, exactly as printed: a blown save for Jim Brewer (he entered with a 3-1 lead in the bottom of the 6th and surrendered the go-ahead runs on Bonds's three-run home run; the app charges the blown save to the reliever who gives up the lead, the established app pattern); inherited runners for Brewer 2/2 (Fletcher, hit by Koufax's pitch, and Mays, walked by Koufax, both aboard when Brewer relieved with none out in the bottom of the 6th, both scoring on the Bonds home run) and for Romo 1/1 (Snider, Mathewson's runner at second when Romo relieved with two out in the top of the 6th, scoring on Hodges's double).
